claims.text: Replica-exchange molecular dynamics combined with thermodynamic integration can accurately determine melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties for high-entropy alloys.
The combined replica-exchange and thermodynamic-integration framework will determine these properties efficiently.
The proposed simulations will operate near melting across a diverse range of high-entropy-alloy compositions.
The simulations will be calibrated against high-precision calorimetric benchmarks and binary or ternary alloy data.
Accurate mapping of the free-energy landscape enables prediction of phase transitions and melting-related thermodynamic properties.
Enhanced temperature and compositional sampling produces an accurate map of the high-entropy-alloy free-energy landscape.
Replica-exchange molecular dynamics efficiently traverses the complex configurational space of high-entropy alloys.
Thermodynamic integration computes the free-energy differences associated with phase transitions.
Combining replica exchange with thermodynamic integration captures the atomic-scale fluctuations and structural reorganizations governing melting.
The method will predict melting temperatures and associated thermodynamic properties within approximately 5% of experimental calorimetric benchmarks.
Simplified models and standard molecular dynamics often suffer from limited sampling of compositional complexity and temperature-driven fluctuations.
The approach is expected to be reliable for high-entropy alloys that do not undergo severe phase segregation or decomposition before melting.
Applicability under extreme compositional or kinetic conditions has not been fully validated.
Exceptionally complex phase behavior or non-equilibrium structural states may reduce the precision of the method.
Consistent deviations greater than 5% from experimental measurements across a statistically significant set of alloy compositions would falsify the proposed approach.
